subject.title: Text overlap rendering bug in Telegram inline keyboard messages (macOS desktop app)

question: Should the canonical fix be a targeted repair to the actual `/model` and `/commands` Telegram callback/message paths, or should OpenClaw accept a broader Telegram rendering/config change such as raw mode or global rich-heading flattening?
rationale: The linked candidate PRs show competing fix shapes, one adding config surface and one changing rich-heading semantics, while the reported paths are specific callback and command-list surfaces that still need focused proof.

options.title: Retarget to reported paths
options.body: Patch the concrete command-list/model-picker rendering path and require native Telegram Desktop proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Approve broader render behavior
options.body: Accept a raw-mode or global rich-heading change only with explicit compatibility rationale, full path wiring, metadata/docs/tests if config is added, and focused proof.

options.title: Pause candidate PRs
options.body: Leave this issue open and close or pause unsuitable candidates until a contributor can provide a focused repair with proof.

recommendation.title: Retarget to reported paths
recommendation.body: Patch the concrete command-list/model-picker rendering path and require native Telegram Desktop proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the Telegram rich-message compatibility/default boundary that both linked candidate fix shapes would extend or bypass.
